newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-GRADY, CAMPBELL AMONG OPEN QUALIFIERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GRADY, CAMPBELL AMONG OPEN QUALIFIERS.

text.p: Australian Wayne Grady and Michael Campbell of New Zealand, who have both come close to winning the British Open, will have to survive final qualifying to play in next month's championship at Royal Troon.
The Royal and Ancient Club, who run the Open, said the two would both have to play in 36-hole qualification tournaments on July 13 and 14 because they were not exempt.
Grady, 39, was beaten by American Mark Calcavecchia in a three-man play-off which also included Greg Norman to decide the title when the championship was last played at Troon in 1989.

Campbell finished joint third at St Andrews in 1995 after leading following a brilliant third round of 65 which included a near-impossible shot out of the famous "Road Hole" bunker on the 17th hole. The title was won by American John Daly after a play-off against Costantino Rocca of Italy.
